summary: Coeur d'Alene forest lookout on the Blacktail ridge: 1927 cabin, 1936 40-foot L-4 tower, destroyed 1947. Hike-in site; no remains of the cabin or tower described.

facts.status_note: Tower destroyed in 1947. No source describes what remains of the cabin or tower; one photo caption says trees overgrow the views from the Butler Mountain lookout site.

visit.trail_note: Drive up Blacktail Road to NF 230, then hike from the Maiden Rock Trailhead; the ridge leads left to Butler or right to Blacktail.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Two Blacktail Mountain lookouts appear in Bonner County. The 1936 40-foot tower and the 1947 destruction match this record. The 1932 10-foot tower, 1941 destruction and Kaniksu National Forest site near Nordman belong to a different lookout.
The 1931 record names the Pend Oreille National Forest, now part of the Idaho Panhandle National Forests. The tower-era list names the Coeur d'Alene National Forest.
Not resolved: the federal record gives 23 and the local history gives 19. The story reports both and does not choose one.

sources.title: Blacktail Lookout Hit by Lightning Fatality 1931

notes_for_editor: Record point (48.1188, -116.51881) is labelled Blacktail Mountain, but the cabin and tower are placed on Butler Mountain at the north end of the Blacktail ridge; check which summit the point sits on. The 1931 death is dated June 21 (lessons record) and June 23 (the local history's passage). The age is 23 (lessons record) or 19 (local history), and the first name is Glen, Ben or James. The local history's June 23 passage carries no quotation marks and names no newspaper on the page, so the story does not call it a newspaper quote. The Kaniksu site's staff (Ivan Painter 1934, Bill Stobie 1936) and its 2024 visit report are left out because they belong to the other lookout. No source describes the remains of the cabin or tower. The only present-day details are the hiking route and one photo caption saying trees overgrow the views from the Butler Mountain site.
